title: U-net skip connections between encoder and decoder halves
description: Added 4 zero-init learnable-gated skips (layers 4,5,6,7 each add the output of layer 3,2,1,0) plus a skip_lambdas parameter trained in the x0 scalar AdamW group; 13 lines, no other change.
reflection: Negative result: val_bpb 1.001167 vs baseline 0.997333 (+0.0038), i.e. a clear regression, not a wash. Throughput was unaffected (MFU 38.7%, 927 steps, 486M tokens, 45.1GB VRAM), so the cost is purely representational/optimization, not speed. The lesson I'd draw: U-net skips are a canonical modded-nanogpt win, but they do NOT transfer to this architecture, which already has two cross-layer shortcut mechanisms -- per-layer x0 injection (x0_lambdas) and value embeddings on alternating layers. Adding a third path appears to be redundant capacity that only adds gradient interference. Zero-init made it identity at step 0, so the regression is the optimizer actively moving skip_lambdas somewhere harmful (scalar_lr=0.5 with betas (0.96,0.95) lets them move fast). I would not spend another run rescuing this with a smaller scalar LR or fewer skips -- the effect size is in the wrong direction and the mechanism is already covered. Broader takeaway for the cell: the 'add another residual/shortcut path' region of the search space looks saturated in this codebase; the untouched regions I'd bet on instead are head count (HEAD_DIM=128 gives only 4 heads at dim 512) and the parameter allocation imbalance (~67M in value-embedding tables vs ~25M in transformer matrices).
